newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed Monday below New York's previous finish on overseas sales after a day of lacklustre trade, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$354.90/355.40 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$355.30/80 close on Friday.
Some dealers said sales came from Australia, as producers launched hedging programs, but noted it was not a big amount.
The market continued to look weak with the prospect of central bank sales still casting its shadow, and dealers expected gold to test the downside between $348 and $350 per ounce.
The shortage of gold bars in Hong Kong continued and premiums inched up to 160 U.S. cents on Monday, up from 150 U.S. cents last week, bullion dealers said.
But jewellery manufacturers had no choice as demand was heating in the run-up to Chinese Lunar New Year in February.
"This is the period of heaviest demand," said one trader.
Local gold ended HK$7 lower at HK$3,278 a tael.
The carry over charges per ten taels at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.50 from their previous fix on Saturday at -5.90.
